$meta.declares: SEL-1 SP schedule-axis offline-profile measurement cache (C3' capability-keyed pattern library, measurement layer): SP4 output-tiling (measurements) + M1c loop-order (loop_order_measurements)
$meta.note: The [SEL-1] measurement library: the OFFLINE-PROFILE cache the capability-keyed SP4 (tiled-vs-plain) tiling selector consults BEFORE its cold-start [XFER-1] prior. Each row memoizes the byte-exact-gated timing of ONE (declared_instance_hash, kernel, variant) instance. This is EVIDENCE-axis mirror data (core-invariants I4): it NEVER chooses route/compute/dtype and it is NEVER a correctness or cost authority in `lib/` -- a measured timing is a cache FACT (authority order: hardware measurement > this cache > static prior). The compiler holds an in-memory VIEW of this file (plugin/rvv RVVRepackTilingSelection.h lookupTilingMeasurement) and, on a HIT for (declared_instance_hash, kernel), picks the memoized argmin variant with reason=measured; on a MISS it falls to the [XFER-1] capability prior (reason=prior).
$meta.seed_state: SEEDED (T3): the 5 K-quant GEMM leaves from the REAL T8 rvv/VLEN128 board (experiments/active/result-tables/T8_winloss_gap_ledger.csv, the [XFER-1] tiling win/loss rows), keyed on the declared_instance_hash the @rvv fixture kernels expand to (3cd23a4e..., the SAME support::computeDeclaredInstanceHash the exec/schedule attribution sinks compute). q4_0 and the iq4 codebook pair carry NO seed row => the compiler cold-starts them via the [XFER-1] prior (reason=prior). A different (un-profiled) board hashes differently => a MISS => the prior. An offline-profile harness on `ssh rvv` fills a row ONLY after the candidate compiles, runs (micro / llama-bench), and PASSES the byte-exact gate for that instance.

key_semantics.declared_instance_hash: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the EXPANDED normalized capability fact set -- the SAME support::computeDeclaredInstanceHash the [D-4](1) exec / schedule attribution sinks compute (one helper, one hash). Portable across symbol renames; profile-vs-explicit-list declarations hash equal. The seed rows carry the @rvv fixture instance's hash (3cd23a4e...).
key_semantics.kernel: the decode_model (the SP4 tiling leaf identity), e.g. "q4_K". NOTE the SELECTION keys on the bottleneck SHAPE (fold_model), NEVER this format name; `kernel` is only the measurement-row identity, not a dispatch key.

$meta.decision_rule: The memoized winner of a (declared_instance_hash, kernel) group is the byte-exact-gated variant that REACHES the <=32-vreg register cliff (register_cliff_reached: spill->0, maxVreg <= v30) AND is decisively faster; else the SIMPLER variant (plain) per 更简单者胜. So a MARGINAL non-cliff wall shave does NOT flip the winner to s6_tiled: q3_K's tiled +8% is a byte-exact overhead-shave that neither reaches the cliff (v31) nor flips its ~5.2x vs-block-dot loss, so the honest measured winner is plain (a weight-bound NULL-lever fallback). This is the [XFER-1] transfer-boundary claim recorded as data: measurement itself says 'do not tile here'.

value_shape.selected: true on the winning variant of its (declared_instance_hash, kernel) group (the memoized argmin the in-memory view returns); false on the runner-up.
value_shape.register_cliff_reached: true iff the S6 stack-panel drove hot-loop live-value spill to 0 and maxVreg <= v30 (the <=32-vreg cliff) for this variant -- the structural decision gate.
value_shape.vs_ggml_blockdot_ratio: measured speedup of this variant vs the REAL-dispatched ggml factory block-dot (>1 = our kernel faster). Board rvv/VLEN128, single core. ***[CASE-COMPILER-ASYMMETRY 2026-07-10] CAVEAT***: the opponent here = board-SHIPPED libggml-cpu.so (rvv board = GCC-15) while ours = clang-17 => this ratio is a clang-ours-vs-gcc-shipped COMPILER-ASYMMETRY artifact, NOT a same-compiler kernel-quality result. Symmetric gcc/gcc remeasure EVAPORATES the seed values (q4_K 1.884->0.272, q2_K 1.413->0.386, q5_K 2.193->0.775). This field is a KERNEL-ACCOUNT-WITHDRAWN成色 note ONLY; the SELECTOR never keys on it (see case_compiler_asymmetry.selector_unaffected).
value_shape.ab_wall_ratio_tiled_over_untiled: the paired-cold A/B wall-time ratio s6_tiled/plain (>1 = s6_tiled faster). Recorded on the group, mirrored on both rows. NOTE: both legs are OURS-clang (internal PRE/POST) => compiler-SYMMETRIC => this ratio SURVIVES [CASE-COMPILER-ASYMMETRY] and is a valid selection input.

board_identity.vreg_count: architectural vector register count (32 for rvv1.0).
board_identity.march: the -march the measurement was taken under (rv64gcv).
board_identity.toolchain: ***[CASE-COMPILER-ASYMMETRY 2026-07-10] deployment-toolchain dimension*** (now part of the measurement key). {ours, opp_shipped}: for the rvv/VLEN128 seed rows ours=clang-17, opp_shipped=gcc-15 (board's shipped ggml). A vs_ggml_blockdot_ratio is only same-compiler-valid when ours==opp_shipped; when they differ it is a system-account observation (clang-domain codegen), not a kernel-account beat.

value_shape.byte_exact_gate: "pass" -- a row is written ONLY past the byte-exact gate (fail-closed: an un-gated timing is never cached; both variants are bit-identical vs the construction oracle).
value_shape.source: the T8 ledger row + originating commit the measurement is transcribed from.
value_shape.ts: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the measurement (sentinel "0" for the transcribed seed rows).

$meta.fail_closed_revalidate: The selector discards a cached winner that is no longer feasible under the current capability facts (Stage-1 legality re-check) and falls back to the prior -- a stale cache never forces an infeasible variant.

case_compiler_asymmetry.finding: The seed vs_ggml_blockdot_ratio values on the rvv/VLEN128 s6_tiled rows (q4_K 1.884, q2_K 1.413, q5_K 2.193) are clang-ours(-O2)-vs-gcc-shipped-block-dot COMPILER-ASYMMETRY artifacts. Symmetric gcc/gcc remeasure evaporates them to LOSS (0.272 / 0.386 / 0.775; q5_K-L1 1.5-1.62->0.120). The rvv board ships a GCC-15-compiled ggml; ours is clang-17. gcc 820-vsetvli/742-spill vs clang 71/3-spill = the 5.6x codegen gap that manufactured the apparent win.
case_compiler_asymmetry.selector_unaffected: THE SELECTION IS UNAFFECTED. SP4 (tiled-vs-plain) keys on register_cliff_reached (spill->0, maxVreg<=v30 = objdump/codegen fact, compiler-symmetric) AND the internal ab_wall_ratio_tiled_over_untiled (both legs ours-clang, compiler-symmetric). It NEVER keys on vs_ggml_blockdot_ratio. So the memoized argmin winner (s6_tiled where the cliff is reached) is correct regardless of the artifact; vs_ggml_blockdot_ratio is a成色/reporting note only.
case_compiler_asymmetry.double_ledger: kernel-account (source-quality claim) = compiler-symmetry FORCED; system-account (product comparison) = each side own full stack + toolchain disclosure + strongest-baseline column. Deployment SOP: ship clang .o object export (front door); never inject our .inc into the opponent's gcc build chain. See (归档·git show pre-restructure-snapshot:(归档·git show pre-restructure-snapshot:docs/canon/Weft-RV_执行总纲v2.md)) §7 items 4/5.
case_compiler_asymmetry.k1_reversal: On k1/VLEN256 the shipped ggml is CLANG-18 (CMakeCache + objdump 19/0 four-proof), so k1 kernel-axis 3.106x/1.916x are ALREADY symmetric-clang and SURVIVE as as-shipped micro beats (NON-e2e). Discriminator key = board-shipped compiler (rvv=gcc, k1=clang).

loop_order_axis.note: The SECOND SP schedule axis the capability-keyed selector consults: the repack PREFILL-GEMM OUTER group-loop ORDER (col_outer / row_outer). The two group loops (activation ROW-group nr/4, weight COLUMN-group nc/16) are INDEPENDENT -- each out[y,x] is a private K-accumulation -- so the orders are BYTE-IDENTICAL and share an identical hot inner core; WHICH is outer is a pure SCHEDULE choice. Lifted (M1c) from the M1b emitter-inlined `weightStride >= activationStride` predicate to a first-class selector axis (RVVRepackTilingSelection.h selectRepackLoopOrder), stamped weft_rvv.loop_order and REALIZED by the EmitC emitter's q4_K min-fold GEMM two-arm body. The rows below live in loop_order_measurements (NOT measurements); the in-memory view is lookupLoopOrderMeasurement.
loop_order_axis.selection_key: The SELECTION keys on the repack LAYOUT STRIDE fact (repackColGroupOuterForLayout: weightStride >= activationStride => col_outer, hold the larger x16-interleaved weight panel loop-resident) + the e2e REGIME (only the two-group prefill GEMM affords the axis; decode GEVM has a single row group), NEVER the format name. So the key MIGRATES across formats with zero per-format entries (换键不改条目). The compiler-symmetric A/B schedule ratio (ab_schedule_ratio_colouter_over_rowouter, both legs ours-clang) is the valid selection input; the system-account absolutes (vs_blockdot_shipped_ratio / vs_upstream_stock_ratio) are DISCLOSURE-only成色 notes the selector never keys on.
loop_order_axis.decision_rule: The memoized winner of a (declared_instance_hash, kernel) group is the order that holds the larger repacked stream loop-resident AND is measured decisively faster (paired-cold A/B). For q4_K on rvv/VLEN128 the weight x16 panel (2304 B) > the activation x4 panel (1168 B) => col_outer, measured 2.47x throughput over row_outer => col_outer is the seeded winner. Only q4_K is A/B loop-interchange-profiled this round; the other repack GEMM leaves cold-start the layout prior (reason=prior).
loop_order_axis.case_compiler_asymmetry: SAME double-ledger discipline as the SP4 axis. The kernel-account selection input ab_schedule_ratio_colouter_over_rowouter is compiler-SYMMETRIC (both legs ours-clang, byte-exact hot core -- only the loop scaffold differs) so it SURVIVES [CASE-COMPILER-ASYMMETRY] and is a valid before/after schedule win. The absolute vs_blockdot_shipped_ratio (1.87x, vs the board-SHIPPED gcc-15 block-dot with q4_K-repack OFF) and vs_upstream_stock_ratio (1.33x, vs native gcc-15 llama.cpp) are clang-ours-vs-gcc-shipped SYSTEM-account observations pending a clang-symmetric block-dot remeasure -- toolchain-disclosed, never a kernel-account beat and never a selection input.
